tagline: Wagon repairs and cabins for the motor age.
intro: The byway leaves I-80 at Exit 34 and rejoins it at Exit 48, a loop through Fort Bridger, Urie and Lyman, towns the interstate bypassed when it was built. For a century the valley was a crossroads for the Oregon and Mormon trails, the Pony Express, the transcontinental railroad and the Lincoln Highway.
Jim Bridger's trading post was not much admired in its day. Travelers complained it was overpriced and short of supplies, though many of them made use of its blacksmith's shop.

moments.title: Fort Bridger
moments.text: The trading post has been reconstructed, along with buildings from the later military post and a museum.

moments.title: Black and Orange Cabins
moments.text: Built in 1925 for motorists on the Lincoln Highway, the cabins took guests only until 1936, sat abandoned from 1948 to 1996 and were restored by the state by 2009.

moments.title: Lyman
moments.text: The privately owned Mountain Skies Observatory here is used by the Bridger Valley Astronomical Society.
